rows.estimation_basis: Estimates are directly benchmarked against reference project 'Fleet Tracking Portal for a Logistics Operator' (id=001-logistics-fleet-portal, 3000 total hours across 20 weeks). Downward adjustments were applied to the integration layer (reduced from 520h to ~300h) because the client integrates a single IoT hardware vendor rather than three disparate telematics providers. Map and vehicle CRUD estimates were adjusted from 420h/240h to ~360h/integrated inventory effort reflecting an 800-scooter fleet across 4 fixed municipal boundaries without complex driver dispatch workflows. The alerts engine was calibrated against the reference's route deviation/idle engine (380h historical vs 300-380h here) to cover PostGIS polygon evaluations and idle duration logic. QA, DevOps, and project stabilization were scaled proportionately to ensure production reliability, yielding a total delivery timeframe of approximately 16 calendar weeks.

Estimates are strictly anchored in historical delivery data from 'B2B Marketplace for Industrial Parts' (id=003-ecommerce-b2b-marketplace, 6,100 total hours across 30 weeks). Matching functional modules were benchmarked directly: Catalogue import pipeline (520-620h vs 620h ref), Elasticsearch search & filtering (440-540h vs 540h ref), Customer-specific pricing (650-760h vs 780h ref), Cart/checkout/Stripe Connect split payments (600-720h vs 700h ref), Supplier portal for inventory, orders, and payouts (680-820h vs 820h ref), Admin back-office (420-500h vs 520h ref), DevOps & load testing (320-400h vs 380h ref), and QA/UAT (780-900h vs 920h ref). Adjustments include the exclusion of enterprise punch-out integrations (cXML/OCI: 480h in reference), replaced by an explicit Buyer Order Portal (360-440h) tailored to restaurant managers. Total estimated hours span 5,010 to 6,000 engineering hours, yielding a realistic 26-week delivery roadmap for a multi-disciplinary squad.

Estimates are directly derived from reference project 'Embedded Analytics Dashboard for a SaaS Product' (id=006-saas-analytics-dashboard, 4600 total hours, 24 weeks). The scope matches the reference benchmark across all functional domains: Kafka event streaming (ref: 520 h vs est: 480-560 h), ClickHouse OLAP modeling (ref: 640 h vs est: 600-680 h), tenant-isolated query APIs (ref: 560 h vs est: 520-600 h), drag-and-drop Angular dashboard builder (ref: 1000 h vs est: 920-1080 h), scheduled PDF/email reports (ref: 380 h vs est: 350-420 h), Terraform/DevOps (ref: 440 h vs est: 400-480 h), load testing (ref: 300 h vs est: 280-340 h), and QA/rollout (ref: 760 h vs est: 700-820 h). Total delivery spans 4050 to 4980 hours (midpoint 4515 hours), realistically aligned with reference historical velocity.

Estimates are grounded in reference project 'Internal HR Knowledge Assistant (RAG)' (id=005-hr-internal-ai-assistant; 1,500 total hours, 10 weeks), which implemented a 400-document RAG solution with Angular, FastAPI, Qdrant, citations, and role-based access filtering. Scope was adjusted upwards to accommodate 600 documents (240-280h ingestion), enhanced dual-partition security to ensure staff-only materials are strictly inaccessible to public applicants (180-220h access control), and comprehensive regression evaluation and prompt-injection testing (160-200h evals, 240-290h QA/UAT). Total delivery effort spans discovery, build, security verification, and university UAT over 11 weeks.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against historical delivery data from Reference Project 'KYC Onboarding Platform for a Digital Bank' (id=002-fintech-kyc-onboarding, 5,200 total hours, 26 weeks). The requirements for borrower ID/address capture, third-party ID verification, sanctions/PEP screening, underwriter manual queue, audit trails, GDPR compliance, and regulatory sign-off correspond precisely to the reference project scope. Individual module estimates reflect historical actuals with a reasonable min/max variance band: borrower wizard (440-520h vs 480h ref), ID verification integration (420-500h vs 460h ref), sanctions screening (310-380h vs 340h ref), underwriter review console (680-780h vs 720h ref), rules engine (520-620h vs 560h ref), PII/GDPR retention (380-460h vs 420h ref), audit/reporting (350-420h vs 380h ref), infrastructure/security hardening (580-700h vs 640h ref), and QA/regulatory sign-off (1,100-1,300h vs 1,200h ref).

Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project 004-healthcare-patient-app (3,900 hours, 22 weeks). Analogous modules were mapped directly: the Patient Mobile App (900h) informs the Pet Owner Mobile App (780-920h); the Appointment Scheduling engine (520h) aligns with the Multi-Clinic Scheduling engine (480-560h); Secure messaging and notifications (420h) informs Omnichannel Reminders (360-440h); and the Doctor Web Dashboard (560h) corresponds to the Staff Web Dashboard (500-600h). Video consultation scope (380h) was removed as it was not requested; in its place, custom domain-specific modules were estimated bottom-up: Veterinary EMR (520-640h), Stock/Inventory with Low-Stock Warnings (380-460h), and Invoicing/Billing (340-420h). Overall timeline spans 23 weeks across overlapping discovery, sprint development, QA, and store rollout phases.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project 008-mobile-field-service (3,600 total hours over 21 weeks). The offline data layer with conflict resolution (680-760h) and the checklist/form interface (460-540h) map directly to the reference's offline sync (760h) and job forms (520h). Media capture and digital signature (280-340h) mirror the reference's photo/signature module (300h). Scope adjustments were made by replacing the legacy ERP integration (520h) and dispatch console (640h) with the Head Office Safety Incident Register and Approval Workflow (420-500h) and the Monthly Site Analytics module (260-320h). DevOps (220-280h) and QA/Field Pilot (360-440h) are grounded in the reference's historical allocation for field device stability and offline validation.

Estimates are grounded in reference project '007-edtech-lms' (Corporate LMS; total 2,800 hours over 18 weeks). The base LMS features (core multi-tenant structure, video lesson tracking, quizzes, certificates, and HR manager reporting) match the reference project's functionality and account for approximately 1,600 to 1,900 hours, adjusted slightly downward by removing legacy SCORM support. To accommodate the new requirements, dedicated scope was added for the AI speaking practice subsystem: browser-based audio capture, asynchronous speech evaluation pipeline, and word-level phoneme feedback UI (+700 to 940 hours), alongside mandatory DevOps, automated QA, and launch stabilization. The total effort scales to 2,340-3,100 hours delivered over 20 weeks by a cross-functional squad.

Estimates are directly grounded in Reference Project 005 (Internal HR Knowledge Assistant, 1,500 total hours over 10 weeks). Core RAG capabilities (document ingestion, hybrid retrieval/reranking, streaming citation UI, quality evaluation, monitoring, and QA/UAT) map closely to historical baseline hours. Adjustments were applied for client-specific scope variations: the internal document ACL permissions (180h in reference) were omitted as help-center articles are public/customer-facing. That effort was reallocated towards two critical custom modules: third-party Zendesk ticketing and context escalation (190-240h) and the support lead Knowledge Gap clustering and reporting dashboard (160-200h).

No reference projects were provided. The estimate is based on general experience only, using a bottom-up modular decomposition across mobile frontend, admin web portal, API backend, QA, and cloud infrastructure.

No reference projects were provided for this proposal. The estimates have been built bottom-up from standard enterprise software delivery practices and historical benchmarks for secure multi-tenant financial SaaS applications. The figures account for full software delivery lifecycle effort (inclusive of UX design, backend and frontend development, integration testing, code reviews, automated CI/CD setup, manual QA, and deployment stabilisation). Due to the absence of empirical baseline references, an uncertainty factor of approximately 25-30% is reflected in the spread between minimum and maximum hours.
